item.title: Warner Bros. has posted a social media ad highlighting the deeply divided critical response to Tom Cruise and director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s new film Digger just hours after the review embargo was lifted.
item.description:
Well, that was fast. Warner Bros. has posted a social media ad highlighting the deeply divided critical response to Tom Cruise and director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s new film Digger just hours after the review embargo was lifted.
The movie, which opens in theaters October 2, currently has a “rotten” score of 52% on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes and a score of 44 on Metacritic. (Cruise’s lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes is Cocktail with 11%.)
As Entertainment Weekly reports:
“The ad begins with a quote from X user @thejonathansim: ‘Digger is an ambitious film sure to polarize audiences.’ It then cuts to a clip from the film featuring Cruise’s Digger Rockwell saying, ‘You know what? F--- those people!’ The rest of the ad shows positive and negative phrases from various reactions to the film flipping back and forth on screen including ‘unpleasant’ and ‘masterpiece,’ ‘baffling’ and ‘brilliant,’ and ‘insufferable’ and ‘magnificent’.”
IGN’s Michael Calabro was on the mixed side in his Digger review, awarding the film an “okay” score of 6 out of 10:
“Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs… Digger is far from a must-watch, and if the trailer has you feeling skeptical, save your money. The theater experience won't change your mind, and the laughs that are there still will be when it hits HBO Max.”
Billed as “a comedy of catastrophic proportions,” the satire stars a nearly unrecognizable Tom Cruise as tycoon Digger Rockwell, whose oil drilling operations spark a global disaster.
Digger opens in theaters October 2.

item.title: Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson is telling fans not to worry about the game after Diablo 5’s announcement sparked concerns about the former title’s lifespan.
item.description:
Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson is telling fans not to worry about the game after Diablo 5’s announcement sparked concerns about the former title’s lifespan.
Diablo 5’s reveal at Blizzcon 2026 left fans equal parts excited and worried. Of course, players were pumped for a new Diablo game — but with Diablo 4 having just launched in 2023, the reveal of a new game so soon felt like a death knell for the one they were still playing.
But Brent Gibson, director of Diablo 4, says there’s nothing to fuss about. Speaking with Icy Veins, Gibson outlined some plans for the game’s future content, saying it will continue to receive support well after 5’s release.
“I have an analogy,” he began. “If you’re wearing a sign in the middle of Times Square saying, ‘The end is nigh,’ the end is not nigh. We have a lot coming. We have [the] Amazon [class] coming down the road. The train isn’t stopping.
“One of the things I love about our world is we are not a series of games. We are a universe. We are even adding to Diablo 2 with the Warlock. It’s one of the few franchises where we have the luxury of continued play, and we know our communities.
“If you’re worried, don’t sweat it, because we’re going to be making content for a long time. But we are excited about Diablo 5. We’ve got a show coming. Gone are the years of waiting a decade for more content. It’s a great place to be.”
More specifically, Gibson said Blizzard is planning on supporting seasons for Diablo 4 “as long as the community continues to show up” for it, specifically mentioning the ongoing support for Diablo 2 and Diablo 3.
“There are still people who play those games, and as long as you’re showing up, we’re going to continue to be making content," he assured.
As Gibson mentioned, Diablo 4 is getting the Amazon class in the first half of 2027. With three more years to go until Diablo 5 is released, there’s still plenty of time for developers to flesh out the title with even more classes and experiences — something they spoke about during a dedicated Diablo panel at Blizzcon this year.
“Diablo 4 has bright support,” Diablo 5 director Joe Shely said. “It's fully supported by the team. We were just announcing earlier today, coming to Diablo 4, the Amazon, the Season of Hell's legacy, Diablo 4 is coming to Switch 2, and there will continue to be ongoing support for Diablo 4. There's many reasons for players to keep playing.”
“We have dedicated teams for each of those games because those games are important to us and they're really important for our community,” production director Tiffany Wat added. “I think it really gives us a really great opportunity to be able to collaborate together, to talk with one another. Even though we might be distinct teams, we still work together quite closely because ultimately we are making games for the Diablo community. I think it's the best time to be a Diablo fan.”
For more Diablo news, you can check out our interview with the developers here, as well as catch up with their reaction to the series' animated show coming to Netflix.

item.title: David Jaffe, the creator, co-writer, and director for the original God of War game, has cleared up his viral comments about Ariel Lawrence, creative director for Laufey.
item.description:
David Jaffe, the creator, co-writer, and director for the original God of War game, has cleared up his viral comments about Ariel Lawrence, creative director for Laufey.
Ariel Lawrence has been with the God of War franchise since its very first game — but creator David Jaffe, who left the series behind in 2007 to form his own studio, says he never got along with her during his time at Santa Monica Studio.
He described their contentious work relationship in a September 2026 live stream while reacting to footage for God of War Laufey, where he claimed their personalities clashed and that he didn’t feel as though she was truly passionate about the games they were making.
“I have no problem with female directors at all,” he began. “This woman started as an assistant producer back when we were making the first God of War. Her and I never got along. She thought I was kind of obnoxious and I thought she was pretentious. She didn’t put the audience first.
“People that I didn’t get along with on God of War were people, in my opinion, who were more about, ‘I wanna do well in the corporate world… I want to play the game,’ versus, ‘I’m here with a vision and I will f**kin’ fight you for that vision.’ There was a lack of passion I felt from her, and she was also kind of a judgy asshole, to me.”
Jaffe also slammed Cory Barlog for making Laufey in the first place — which he called a “stupid” game — and asked why he couldn’t “sit Ariel down and say, ‘This isn’t ready.’”
pic.twitter.com/xkPvif83KY
Jaffe’s comments unsurprisingly went viral, sparking a debate within the God of War fanbase and the broader gaming community in general. Not long afterward, Jaffe took to Twitter/X to expound upon his remarks, where he called out those using his statement to harass Lawrence online.
“Look, I personally didn't like Ariel and I don't THINK she cared much for me back when we worked together. Oil and Water, just very different types of people. And honestly, she was probably more liked on the team than I was. You see, if you haven't noticed, I can be, as my ex-wife says, 'a lot,’” he wrote.
“And so in this video, I was responding/sharing that aspect of our time working together. That's the only way I would ever talk about former colleagues, be it good or bad experiences. For people to use my experience with Ariel as an excuse/launching pad to make personal attacks on her is just low and s**tty.
"She's a real person — just like you — with a life and feelings and people who care for her and who love her, and it just seems really f**king cruel to do that. Plus, have you looked in your own mirror? I've looked in mine; that s**t's scary! You see this f**king beard?!? Good lord, I'm days away from moving to the North Pole…”
Look, I personally didn't like Ariel and I don't THINK she cared much for me back when we worked together. Oil and Water, just very different types of people. And honestly, she was probably more liked on the team than I was. You see, if you haven't noticed, I can be, as my… https://t.co/kw0g4JGnMf
Laufey has, unfortunately, been a target for the online rage machine, and Jaffe's remarks are adding more fuel to the fire. Trolls’ remarks about Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance and their outrage over the fact that a woman is leading a God of War game totally overwhelmed gaming circles on social media when it was first revealed in June, and this finger-pointing doesn’t appear to have stopped, but rather simply slowed down.
Other games have since taken the brunt of the internet’s apparent boredom, as evidenced by the debate surrounding Insomniac’s Wolverine. But still, Laufey has managed to catch strays in this regard, with The Last of Us director Bruce Straley using it as an example of why modern AAA games no longer “excite” him (though he later apologized for this comment).
God of War Laufey releases on February 16, 2027, exclusively for PlayStation 5.

item.title: GTA 6 may not even be eligible for Game of the Year at The Game Awards this year.
item.description:
GTA 6 may not even be eligible for Game of the Year at The Game Awards this year.
Actress, games writer, and former games journalist Alanah Pearce stated during a recent live stream that she doesn't think GTA 6 has a good chance of sweeping at The Game Awards this year due to the timing of its release. Pearce stated that the cutoff date for games being eligible for TGA nominations has historically taken place around the same time as GTA 6's release date this year. And while some have countered her insights by noting that the cutoff last year was November 21, two days after GTA 6 will release this year, there are still some valid questions raised.
Most notably: Would anyone even be able to feasibly finish GTA 6 before voting on nominees? And if not, would the jury be willing to vote on it without finishing it? That would certainly raise a lot of ethical concerns over the voting process. However, there are some ways that Rockstar's chances could be increased. For starters, Geoff Keighley, the overseer of The Game Awards, could simply push the voting deadlines back. It's certainly not impossible, as Keighley does love a good show, and GTA 6 sweeping would lead to a lot of eyes on the event.
Another possibility is that Rockstar Games could give jury members a significant headstart to play the game prior to the cutoff date. As of right now, it's hard to say what Rockstar's plans are for reviewers, but such a strategy would certainly give it an easier time securing a nomination. It's a lot of ifs, though.
We can only speculate, but if for whatever reason GTA 6 isn't eligible this year, it could try again in 2027... and it might still have a chance. Rockstar Games is heavily rumored to launch GTA 6's online mode next year, which will undoubtedly give the game a massive second wind. If that's enough to contend with other heavy hitters, such as Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, Rockstar could be in the 2027 awards race.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: 007 First Light is getting new, free DLC later this week.
item.description:
007 First Light is getting new, free DLC later this week.
IO Interactive has teased the new DLC via a short video on its socials, confirming it will arrive on Thursday, October 2. The DLC will be free, but as of right now, IO is remaining tight-lipped about what it will include. However, based on some prior info, we can likely assume that this is the long-awaited Aston Martin Valhalla update. This content has been teased since launch in the game's main menu, and it appears it's finally being added to the game.
This is expected to include a new TacSim mission featuring the Aston Martin Valhalla, which is used near the end of the game as part of a massive set piece. Given the extensive wait, it seems hard to imagine this will be just a short, single TacSim mission. This may add some other items that were revealed as part of a larger roadmap for the game, such as new game+, new gadgets, and other missions and content.
A free DLC is just around the bend. Tune in on October 1st.#007FirstLight #EarnTheNumber pic.twitter.com/9uCpNDTPth
We'll just have to sit tight and wait to see what exactly is in store, though. 007 First Light is also set to get a new story DLC centered around Bawama, the pirate king warlord played by Lenny Kravitz. There's no firm release date for that content, though it's expected to be a premium add-on rather than a free update like what's coming later this week.
007 First Light's Nintendo Switch 2 port is also still coming down the pipeline. It was expected to be out by now, but was recently pushed to 2027 to ensure it was as good as it could be for fans. It's unclear for how long IO Interactive plans to support this game, as it has continued to drop updates for Hitman many years after its release. Even without a steady stream of post-launch content, 007 First Light has been a big hit. The game sold 4 million copies in its first three months, and sequels are expected to follow, though it will likely be a while before they materialize.

item.title: Zach Cregger’s next movie, a science fiction thriller called The Flood, is set to release in theaters on August 11, 2028.
item.description:
Zach Cregger’s next movie, a science fiction thriller called The Flood, is set to release in theaters on August 11, 2028.
Cregger is writing, producing, and directing the film, which will star Jennifer Lawrence, as confirmed by Variety on September 29, 2026.
Warner Bros. and New Line Cinema are slated to distribute the movie, which is being produced by Amblin Entertainment and Vertigo Entertainment's Roy Lee and Miri Yoon.
Thus far, other cast members and specific plot details have been kept secret, but Cregger has given us a few insights into what we can expect from his forthcoming sci-fi flick. Speaking to Men’s Health in mid-September, Cregger revealed that the movie is 'similar' to Stanley Kubrick’s 2001: A Space Odyssey.
“I'm not comparing [The Flood] to 2001, because I think 2001 is a true masterpiece in every sense of the word. But there's a bizarreness to that movie that's really undeniable, and it's also a horror movie. I think 2001 is a really thrilling horror movie about human nature, and obviously about artificial intelligence, but it asks big questions. And I think, in that way, there's some similarity with Flood,” he said.
Based on these remarks, we can safely assume that The Flood has something to do with AI, human nature, and big-picture concepts — but one thing he confirmed was that The Flood is very specifically not a horror movie.
“It unfolds in a very unique way that I'm really proud of. It's disturbing, but it's not a horror movie, although there are horror scenes in it. It feels intimidating to me. I'm still not really sure how to make it, but I think that's a good thing,” he clarified.
“It's hard to talk about it without talking about the story. I’m thrilled to have the opportunity to make that movie. I’m in love with that story in a really unique way."
This news comes hot on the heels of Cregger’s Resident Evil adaptation, which released to overwhelmingly positive reviews among both fans of the games and film critics alike. It became the single most-successful Resident Evil movie ever, and even helped boost sales for Resident Evil 2 Remake by 50% on PlayStation 5.
Cregger is best known for horror flicks like Barbarian and Weapons, so it’ll be interesting to see his take on a science fiction thriller. He isn’t the only big director in the horror space with exciting news to share, either, as Obsession director Curry Barker’s next movie, a horror-comedy titled Anything But Ghosts, has received a theatrical release date for May 7, 2027.

item.title: Obsession director Curry Barker’s next film, Anything But Ghosts, is coming to theaters next year.
item.description:
Obsession director Curry Barker’s next film, Anything But Ghosts, is coming to theaters next year.
Anything But Ghosts comes to the silver screen on May 7, 2027. The film takes place in the same universe as Obsession, but is classified as a horror-comedy that follows a different cast of characters entirely — though they also go through some seriously spooky stuff.
Barker’s next flick stars Bryce Dallas Howard, Aaron Paul, Violet McGraw, Chris Reinache, and Cooper Tomlinson, who notably played Bear’s best friend, Ian, in Obsession, as well as Barker himself. Anything But Ghosts centers around two fake paranormal investigators who are finally confronted with some actual, real-life ghosts (or would that be ‘real-afterlife’ ghosts?), causing things to “spiral wildly and terrifyingly out of control,” as per an official press release.
Speaking on a June episode of Raiders of the Lost Podcast, Tomlinson confirmed that he and Curry are playing the two phony ghost hunters, and described the film as “if Key and Peele walked into Hereditary.”
“It’s a buddy comedy, you know, about these two guys, and it turns really scary,” he said. “You know, it’s about these con artist ghost hunters who encounter real ghosts, and then they have to step up and be the thing that they promised this family.”
Both Barker and Tomlinson are producing and co-writing the film, which is produced by Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster. Focus holds the movie’s worldwide rights, and Universal Pictures International is handling international distribution for the studio. This is the second time Focus and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have worked together on a Curry Barker film; the two production houses also collaborated on Obsession, which released to rave reviews earlier this year.
Barker’s next offering has a lot to live up to; Obsession became one of the world's most profitable films compared to its budget in history, receiving critical acclaim and becoming an instant horror classic. Inde Navarrette’s standout performance as Nikki catapulted her to international fame, helping her land the role of Rogue in Marvel’s X-Men reboot, and put Barker in the hotseat for studios looking to get in on his future projects.
If you’ve ever watched Barker and Tomlinson’s humorous YouTube videos, you can safely assume that their delightful chemistry will get ample time to shine in Anything But Ghosts. With hard-hitters like Breaking Bad’s Aaron Paul and Jurassic World’s Bryce Dallas Howard in the mix, there’s no telling what hijinks these two will get up to, but we can almost guarantee it’ll be hilarious. And given how creepy Obsession managed to be on such a small budget, it feels like the Hereditary-ness of it all might also give us a few good scares, too.
Image Credits: Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images for IMDb

item.title: Coinbase is joining the Pokémon TCG craze with its own digital pack-opening platform.
item.description:
Coinbase is joining the Pokémon TCG craze with its own digital pack-opening platform.
Coinbase, a US-based cryptocurrency exchange platform, is moving in on the TCG market with a particular focus on Pokémon. At least, that’s what it seems like, based on a tweet it published on September 28.
“Your binder is about to get a major upgrade,” the post reads. “Rip packs on your phone. Every pull backed by a real, physical card. Vault it or ship it. Soon on Coinbase.”
Your binder is about to get a major upgrade.Rip packs on your phone.Every pull backed by a real, physical card.Vault it or ship it.Soon on Coinbase. pic.twitter.com/Utfwq30DSj
While the post’s text doesn’t mention Pokémon by name, the accompanying image attached to it shows mockups of five Pokémon TCG card packs that are labeled ‘Pokémon’ with the numbers 1-5.
The platform also responded to a few comments that mentioned the popular monster-catching franchise; one user wrote, “Pokémon packs on the chain, trading cards just hit peak convenience,” to which it replied, “You get it.”
“STFU, Coinbase is going to partner with and onboard everything on earth,” another wrote, to which Coinbase responded, “Well, we are the Everything Exchange.”
Based on this post, it looks like Coinbase users will soon be able to open digital card packs, with the option to place those cards in a digital ‘vault’ or receive their physical equivalent by mail.
However, another reply from Coinbase suggests there’ll be some additional features at play; one user wrote, “The vaulting aspect is the real game changer here,” to which it replied, “And there’s more…”
For now, details remain sparse. We don’t know how Coinbase’s status as a crypto platform will impact its attempt at a pack-opening service, nor how it intends to grade said cards or provide proof of ownership. Will these pulls come from pre-opened packs? Who’s to say.
It’s also worth noting that such a service, sans cryptocurrency, already exists; as pointed out by Dexerto, Gamestop’s Power Packs program also features a digital option, allowing customers to open mystery packs online and receive those cards’ physical counterparts.
Gamestop assures its buyers that every digital pack contains a "real, authenticated item” that they can either hold in their digital PSA vault, have shipped to them, or take advantage of its instant buyback program and use those funds to purchase another card pack. It remains to be seen if Coinbase will provide similar guarantees.
Coinbase’s proposed pack-opening platform comes on the heels of Pokémon’s 30th Anniversary celebration, which has shone a spotlight on the ever-growing hype around the card collecting scene, as well as the scalpers who have caused chaos during its special merchandise and card launches.
For instance, the special 30th Anniversary card pack drops at retailers like Target and other shops prompted long lines outside stores as mobs of fans showed up for the chance at snagging some packs for themselves, with some even ‘reserving’ spots in line by setting out chairs with no one sitting in them.

item.title: A professional Pokémon player is going viral after begging his fellow competitors to keep up with their personal hygiene, claiming he literally threw up at an event due to someone’s stench.
item.description:
A professional Pokémon player is going viral after begging his fellow competitors to keep up with their personal hygiene, claiming he literally threw up at an event due to someone’s stench.
Texas-based Pokémon VGC regional champion Donghun Youm says he lost his lunch at the 2026 Baltimore Regional Championships thanks to a super smelly player.
Youm wrote about his experience in a viral post on Twitter/X, where he begged players to “please take care of [their] personal hygiene.”
Youm said someone at the competition smelled so foul that he literally threw up because of it, and his friends were unable to concentrate on their own matches due to the putrid stench.
“I've had an incident at Baltimore regionals where I had to throw up due to a nearby player's stench,” he said. “My friends and I couldn't focus that round due to how putrid the smell was, and we even told a judge due to it. Like, c'mon man....”
Youm’s post has kicked off a heated discourse about players’ hygiene at competitions, as well as no end of jokes and memes about certain Pokémon attacks that rely on smell to deal damage or inflict adverse status effects. (The ability ‘Stench’ was most popular, as it has a 10% chance of making your opponent flinch when hit by a damaging move.)
Please take care of your personal hygiene. I've had an incident @ Baltimore regionals where I had to throw up due to a nearby player's stench. My friends and I couldn't focus that round due to how putrid the smell was and we even told a judge due to it. Like c'mon man....
“[Washing] should be a requirement to attend an event,” one commenter replied. “People who smell bad should be kicked out.”
“If you can afford a Nintendo Switch, you can afford a $3 stick of deodorant dude,” another said.
This is far from the first time the subject of hygiene has come up regarding in-person gaming events; in June, a card shop in Oregon suspended its Yu-Gi-Oh tournaments after receiving bad reviews and multiple complaints of smelly patrons.
The shop pointed to Konami’s own tournament guidelines, which stipulate that everyone at a Yu-Gi-Oh competition, not just players, must be “clean and wear clean clothing,” or risk being “penalized.”
Pokémon boasts similar rules; the official Play! Pokemon Tournament Rules Handbook includes a section regarding hygiene, which reads, “Individuals are also required to maintain a socially acceptable level of hygiene during the event. Depending on the attire or level of hygiene, the Tournament Organizer may allow for a tournament participant to change or update their personal hygiene and attire and return to the venue.
"If a participant refuses to comply with tournament staff’s requests, this is grounds for removal from the tournament and venue, and the participant must relinquish their badge to tournament staff."
It’s unclear if the stinky player who caused Youm to throw up was penalized. Either way, the incident has sparked renewed calls from community members for their fellow players to keep themselves clean and fresh at competitions to avoid unpleasant situations like this one.

item.title: Frank O'Connor, Halo's Franchise Creative Director for nearly 20 years at 343 Industries/Halo Studios, has weighed in on Halo's future at Activision, suggesting three viable paths forward for Xbox's former biggest franchise.
item.description:
Frank O'Connor, Halo's Franchise Creative Director for nearly 20 years at 343 Industries/Halo Studios (who, fun fact, was once my colleague at Official Xbox Magazine), has weighed in on Halo's future at Activision, suggesting three viable paths forward for Xbox's former biggest franchise.
O'Connor, who moved on from 343 Industries in 2023, was responding to a post on LinkedIn by former Xbox Social Media Manager of Executive Communications Genevieve Harrison about Halo's move to Activision. Harrison was discussing how Activision might approach Halo, and said in part, "Talent is not a SharePoint folder you drag from /Call of Duty into /Halo and wait for the little green checkmark. What Activision does know how to do is run the absolute hell out of a giant franchise. Maybe that operational discipline is exactly what Halo needs. But Activision isn’t riding in to save Xbox either. Microsoft paid $68.7 billion for Activision Blizzard. Activision is Xbox. Maybe it works. I hope it does because I’d love another great Halo game."
O'Connor, who started on the Halo franchise when he left Official Xbox Magazine to join Bungie during Halo 2's development, replied with his thoughts on how the series's next step at its new developer and publisher might go. "There are 3 paths - any one of which COULD be successful," he said. "None of these are easy, guaranteed or necessarily viable: 1. Make a "classic" Halo movement/sandbox/shooter experience tailored to a core audience & scaled to be successful with that core audience and attractive to a broader one so it can grow (not to mention obvious fact that Halo MP is better w. more people playing, by mathematical default).
"2. Make something new, modern that >reinvents< the game/universe in a surprising but fantastic way. An action/sandbox game (maybe it's a new take on the FPS, maybe it's an action RPG but it's fundamentally different) and succeeds with a combination of strong story, IP use and gets a small head start based on curiosity or loyalty.
"3. Translate Halo IP and sandbox into the ATVI comfort zone. Use the player, progression and business models that are proven to work and craft a big annual or semi-annual spectacle and constant content. Pro-Tip: Do NOT tie it to hardware/services launch cycles, do not try to force it into a shape (or aging platform) that it can't fit and do NOT abandon sandbox. Pro-Pro-Tip: Hire Bungie, Halo Studios and other laid off folk who are bursting w. talent and ideas that got nerfed or shut down over the years."
Halo Studios went through a rebranding effort (from 343 Industries), a leadership shakeup, and a pivot to Unreal Engine as its underlying game technology in 2024, and shipped the multiplayer-less remake of the original Halo, called Halo: Campaign Evolved, earlier this year. However, the studio was reportedly years away on its next mainline Halo project ahead of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma and Xbox COO Matt Booty's decision to hand Halo to the House of Call of Duty. I've since written about whether or not Activision can save Halo, but I'm not as convinced on the creative side, while my colleague Matt Purslow wrote about how, no matter what, Halo must go beyond Bungie's original template.
Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked, and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch. He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan.

item.title: Warner Bros. has officially set a June 1, 2029 release date for Game of Thrones: Aegon's Conquest, with Owen Harris attached to direct.
item.description:
Warner Bros. has officially announced a release date and director for Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest, the first feature film to stem from the HBO franchise.
Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest will open in theaters on June 9, 2029. Owen Harris will direct from a screenplay by Beau Willimon (House of Cards). The film will adapt material from George R.R. Martin’s Targaryen history book, Fire & Blood.
Harris is no stranger to Game of Thrones, having directed episodes of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms. Harris also directed three acclaimed episodes of Black Mirror ("Be Right Back", "San Junipero", and "Striking Vipers").
Martin’s Fire & Blood chronicles the history of the dragon-riding Targaryen dynasty, including the Dance of the Dragons civil war depicted in House of the Dragon. The Targaryens arrived in Westeros following the Doom of Valyria, settling on the island of Dragonstone. By the time Aegon reached adulthood, he made it his mission to unite the long-warring Seven Kingdoms under the rule of one man: himself.
Aegon I Targaryen is responsible for countless deaths in his quest to become the sole ruler of the realm. He’s aided by his sister-wives Visenya and Rhaenys. All three siblings fly fearsome dragons: Aegon rides Balerion the Black Dread, Visenya rides Vhagar (yes, the same giant beast flown by Aemond in House of the Dragon), and Rhaenys flies Meraxes.
Aegon battles a slew of kingdoms during the Conquest, but his two biggest adversaries are King Harren the Black, the wicked lord of Harrenhal, and Meria Martell, the princess of Dorne. Meria and Dorne’s resistance against Aegon the Conqueror was notably recalled by Ormund Hightower to Daeron Targaryen in House of the Dragon Season 3, Episode 5.
The Game of Thrones series has established that Aegon knew about the White Walkers and passed this secret knowledge down the generations from ruler to ruler. Aegon foresaw a great looming terror in the North, which convinced him that a Targaryen must occupy the Iron Throne when that dark day arrives to ensure humanity’s survival.
Bringing Aegon’s Conquest to the big screen poses a host of challenges for the filmmakers, several of which I break down here.

item.title: The BBC's new director general has described an AI-generated Doctor Who episode as "pretty good," and suggested that the technology enabled the creation of content "at the standard of a Hollywood studio."
item.description:
The BBC's new director general has described a 50-minute AI-generated episode of Doctor Who as "pretty good," and suggested that the technology now enabled the creation of content "at the standard of a Hollywood studio."
Brittin became boss of the UK's iconic broadcasting company in May this year, after almost two decades at Google, where he wound up working as the company's UK managing director.
Now in charge of the BBC, Brittin faces a tough task of making further drastic cuts to the corporation's spending, while it continues to try and produce world-class programming — including its flagship sci-fi adventure series that's currently on hiatus after a disastrous few years.
Doctor Who fans largely agree that their favorite show has declined in quality over the years, but especially over the past two seasons which featured Ncuti Gatwa in the role, and the return of Russell T Davies as showrunner. After just two seasons, this era of the show was unceremoniously ended when co-funding partner Disney ditched the series, prompting the departure of Gatwa in a reshot ending. A later promise to mount a one-off Christmas special that could tie-up the era's remaining plotlines was later scrapped too, with Davies and production company Bad Wolf also exiting.
Now, the BBC has begun looking for a fresh production house to take the show on — a process it wants to result in new episodes of the series arriving in either 2028 or 2029.
"Somebody sent me a 50-minute episode of Doctor Who that was AI-generated the other day," Brittin said, speaking at the Royal Television Society conference in London this week (thanks, Variety). "It's pretty good. I mean, it's not going to replace humans, and we'll come on to that
"So everyone's a creator. Not all the creativity is bad," Brittin continued. "Everyone's got the ability in their hands — or six billion people have — to create content at the standard of a Hollywood studio."
While Brittin does not name the AI project he watched, it is almost certainly the 50-minute first episode of fan-made project The Unmade Season, which features a AI-made continuation of the series. Having watched a chunk of this myself, I'd say it is as good as you'd expect AI to be — which is to say, almost photorealistic but narratively still pretty flawed. The show picks up with a new incarnation of the Doctor who regenerates from David Tennant's 14th Doctor, played a Scottish-sounding AI actor. Scenes feature various AI oddities, though also incorporate various familiar Doctor Who monsters, such as Slitheen and Ood.
All in all, it's not very good. And as a Doctor Who fan, it is particularly odd to hear the boss of the BBC offering any sort of praise to content, even non-commercial fan content, that appears to have been generated by regurgitating the BBC's own copyrighted episodes.
While budgets may be tight, here's hoping this is the extent of the BBC's relationship to AI with Doctor Who going forward.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: We've rounded up all of the major GTA 6 details revealed in the latest Game Informer cover story.
item.description:
Game Informer's GTA 6 coverage reveal has shed new light on Rockstar's upcoming game, and we've rounded up all the big new information.
In the story, Rockstar shared new details about GTA 6's ambitious weather systems, the wildlife and NPCs that populate the world, and the scope of GTA 6's map.
Rockstar has managed to pull off one of the most speculated parts of GTA 6: hurricanes. Fans were hoping to see Florida's most significant weather event replicated in GTA 6, but given how intense hurricanes are, many wondered if it was even technically feasible. Speaking to Game Informer, Rockstar confirmed they will be featured in the game, but declined to share how often they will happen and if they will impact the story.
As for how they will be depicted, fans can expect “heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics, and a lot of rain combine so that everything is dripping wet, water is gushing off roof edges and lampposts, thunder rumbles and flashes of lightning light up the clouds dramatically.”
Rockstar's VP of art for lighting and rendering, Owen Shepherd, confirmed that the studio re-engineered its weather system to allow for localized, persistent, and dynamic weather. The player can soak up sunny rays in one part of the map, but still be able to see a rainstorm in the distance. The game will also feature rainbows and puddles, allowing the player to travel through an area and deduce that it recently rained there without having been present for it. Additionally, wind will create ripples in the water, blow hair around, and push debris across the world.
Rockstar North co-studio head Aaron Garbut confirmed that GTA 6's map is twice as big as GTA 5's, with an emphasis on density. The setting of the game, as many know, is a fictionalized version of Florida known as Leonida.
"This new world is different," Garbut said. "We obsessed about every part – the rooftops, the alleys, the internals and everything in between to the point we hit a critical mass with the numbers of our interiors, and you start to feel the buildings are more real inside and out. This world is a cohesive whole with the density of content and a hand-crafted quality to every bit."
GTA 6's map will feature six different regions. The most prominent one is Vice City, a location fans are familiar with thanks to 2002's GTA: Vice City. The other regions of Leonida include Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park.
Ambrosia is a more rural part of the map with factories and refineries, dominated by a biker gang who control the area. This gang appears to be different from the Lost MC, which were prominently featured in GTA 4 and GTA 5.
With a map as big as Rockstar is promising, GTA 6 may feel daunting to would-be explorers. However, Rockstar plans to use the game's story to take players around the map and show off the different areas. Of course, this won't cover every inch of the world, but it will demonstrate the strong contrast of more affluent parts of Leonida versus more "poor" areas.
GTA has historically let players hop in a cab to freely fast travel through the world, but Red Dead Redemption 2 was a bit more restrictive. You could fast travel from town to town, but not any hyper specific points on the map. GTA 6 will allow you to hop in a ride share car and zip around town... however, ride sharing means just that: sharing. Players will be able to share rides with other passengers and have unique conversations.
If you don't want to make conversation with other passengers or sightsee, you can doomscroll on Snapmatic, the game's parody of Instagram.
Players won't be able to post on the app themselves, as Jason and Lucia are on the run and would risk danger by being overly active on social media.
GTA 6 will feature a boatload of side activities; here are just some of them, as revealed in Game Informer's story:
• Base Jumping• Billiards• Gyms• Kayaking• Mini Golf• Scuba Diving• Street & Off-Road Racing• Zoos• Air Boating• Jet Skiing
Fans will be able to see and interact with 170 different types of animals. This includes over 60 birds, over 30 land mammals, and a variety of fish and reptiles. The extended gameplay reveal in August confirmed that players will be able to pet dogs and if it's anything like Red Dead Redemption 2, this will presumably extend to other animals like cats.
“Florida has a diverse animal ecosystem that we wanted to faithfully include across the different biomes in Leonida – urban and rural environs, aquatic life both inland and ocean, and the wetland habitats like the swamps and Everglades,” Rockstar vice president of dynamic art, Michael Kane, explained. “The animal art and population teams are incredibly passionate about delivering animals that are accurately researched and look visually correct in every respect, alongside the supporting movement and animation to bring them to life.”
Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 features different shark species, jellyfish, whales, turtles, and rays in the game's sea. They will have "distinct movement behavior" and can be encountered while scuba diving in the water.
One of the screenshots in Game Informer's story shows Jason approaching deer in the wild with a rifle strung over his back. It seems to suggest some form of hunting will return in the game. Hunting was a very small part of GTA 5 and a bit half-baked. The system returned in Red Dead Redemption 2 with significantly more depth.
Players will be able to track animals as they did in Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar also confirmed there will be rare animal types, but didn't reveal any.
Robberies are a central part of the game and players will have a lot of choice in how they do that. Do they go as a duo? Do they go alone? Do they go loud? Do they go quiet? There are a lot of options, but your choices will determine the level of response you can get from the police.
Jason and Lucia can shake the cops together or split up, leaving one person to take the bulk of the heat. However, if either one of these protagonists gets overwhelmed by police, it's game over.
Higher end cars require special tools to steal and if successful, they may have trackers or security systems to create new obstacles for you. Players can use an app known as WAiNK to determine a car's resale value, security system, and the cost to make it your own personal vehicle. Should you want to off-load it, you'll have to take it to a fence.
The two protagonists, Jason and Lucia, may long for a romantic relationship together, but it is up to the player to determine whether or not they go beyond a platonic one. The player will be able to essentially court the two characters by taking them on dates, paying attention when they call or text you, and being chivalrous by opening doors or holding hands.
GTA 6's story will be ripe for multiple playthoughs. Rockstar confirmed that choices big and small with not only influence Jason and Lucia's relationship, but the story as a whole, encouraging players to play the game again to see alternative story threads.
“As the pressure for us on this project is huge, we dealt with that by doing our best to overdeliver," said Rockstar North co-studio head Aaron Garbut. "Normally you compromise scale for detail or detail for interaction, but with this project we went the other way - everything is dialed up – detail, scope, breadth, scale, interaction and density. I don't think we have ever created anything close to this before."
Rockstar has created a wide variety of NPCs that vary in height, weight, skin type, and more. Characters can get a tan, they can have moles, and even the sizes of their butts and chests will vary from person to person.
GTA 6 will feature a ton of clothing options, which players can acquire with their ill-gotten gains. NPCs will also be dressed differently based on where they are in the world. If they're in a more impoverished area, expect them to have dirtier or weathered clothing.
“We’ve been able to really go hard on that with creating the biggest range of garments and accessories we’ve ever made – supported with rich, realistic materials,” Kane says. “That surfacing includes color, patterns and branding that are both area-appropriate, but also tied to context (states of dirt/weathering and fitment) for the characters themselves and their social situation and how they inhabit Leonida. Shoes, sneakers, and colorways that we know carry cultural weight as items – likewise watches, sunglasses, or hats.”
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: It sounds like Grand Theft Auto 6 will take open world weather effects to another level, with simulated tropical storms and hurricanes.
item.description:
It sounds like Grand Theft Auto 6 will take open world weather effects to another level, with simulated tropical storms and hurricanes.
We already knew that GTA 6 would have an advanced weather system of some kind. But in Game Informer's GTA 6 cover story, senior associate editor Marcus Stewart described the need for Leonida to have diverse weather, due to Florida's tendency to have wild shifts in its climate. And, it seems like Rockstar has that covered.
Rockstar vice president of art for lighting and rendering, Owen Shepherd, told Stewart, "We have re-engineered our weather system to make everything much more localized and persistent," and that "the world features new fully dynamic cloudscapes that roll across the map."
We already know that GTA 6 is going to have a map that's three times larger than the ones found in Grand Theft Auto 5 and in Red Dead Redemption 2, so it's even more impressive that the game will be able to simulate moving storm systems. In practice, this will absolutely mean you can get localized rain showers in one area, while the next area is sunny. But while that alone wouldn't necessarily be groundbreaking, it seems like weather systems will have lasting effects on the environment.
According to Stewart, he was told that "GTA 6's rain creates realistic rainbows under the right lighting conditions, and that recently showered areas will remain wet on the ground and create persistent puddles once the storm passes." That'd be cool enough if the weather in Leonida only got as extreme as a thunderstorm but in real life, Florida is known to have more unpredictable weather.
Luckily, GTA 6 will also have simulated tropical storms and hurricanes, which will wreak havoc on the environment. Shepherd says that these storms will have "heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics and a lot of rain combine so that everything is dripping wet, water is gushing off roof edges and lampposts, thunder rumbles and flashes of lighting light up the clouds dramatically."
Unfortunately, Game Informer's cover story doesn't come with video that shows these weather systems in action, but combined with the persistent effects weather can have on the environment, my imagination is running wild. Will there be flooding in the streets? Will buildings and trees get knocked down? There are a ton of possibilities, and I already want to jump in and go storm chasing.
GTA 6 launches on November 19, so we won't have to wait too long to see what the weather can do.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

Foot Locker has revealed a new collaboration between Crocs and the hit anime series Chainsaw Man.
The collaboration includes four new Clog designs and a series of five Jibbitz charms. The Clogs will retail starting at $69.99, and will be available both online and at select Foot Locker locations starting October 27. However, fans can get a sneak peek of the new designs ahead of their wide release at New York Comic Con.
The most expensive Clog design of the bunch, listed at $79.99, quite literally turns Pochita into a Croc. Instead of the usual Croc holes, you get a full Pochita face with a little chainsaw sticking out of his head (and your toes). The extra cost can be explained by this being the only clog in the collection to come in the fuzzy lined design.
Two more standard Clog designs are also inspired by specific characters: Power and Chainsaw Man himself. The Power design is based on the Blood Fiend’s blue cardigan outfit, complete with a fuzzy white heel clasp and her iconic red horns.
Chainsaw Man x Crocs Collection
Chainsaw Man gets, well, a whole lot of chainsaw. A blood-splattered red design shows hints of an engine along the heel and cutting teeth peeking out the front. A jagged cutting chain slices through the front toes, creating a 3D effect similar to the Pochita design.
The fourth and final Clog design features a collage of fan-favorite characters from the first season. The five new Jibbitz charms are also modeled after specific characters, narrowing the list down to Aki, Power, Pochita, Makima, and Denji in his Chainsaw Man form.
Where to Buy: The collection will be available in limited quantities at Foot Locker’s New York Comic Con activation beginning October 8, followed by a wider release in select stores and online at footlocker.com on October 27.
Tatsuki Fujimoto penned his last chapter for the Chainsaw Man manga earlier this year. The ongoing anime adaptation, produced by studio MAPPA, continues to grow in popularity.
We were pretty big fans of Season 1, and the story’s continuation in Chainsaw Man: The Movie - Reze Arc contributed to a record-breaking year at the box office in Japan. The anime series will be returning to a standard episodic format for its next season, titled Assassins Arc, which is currently in production.
Crocs, on the other hand, has been going ham with the collaborations, with recent releases themed after massive franchises like Pokemon and Yu-Gi-Oh.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Control Resonant's director has explained how the team chose to handle exploration in a way that doesn't feel like it is holding the player's hand with things like yellow paint.
item.description:
Control Resonant's director has explained how the team chose to handle exploration in a way that doesn't feel like it is holding the player's hand with things like yellow paint.
For a number of years now, some gamers have begun to feel like games provide players with more guidance than is necessary. One example of this is yellow paint, which basically highlights exactly where the player needs to go during exploration. Critics say that when this sort of navigation aid is heavy handed, it can be distracting and remove a sense of agency. Marvel's Wolverine, for example, was heavily criticized for its "fart gas," a blue mist that Wolverine can sniff out to find his objective. Soon after launch, developer Insomniac added the ability to toggle it off.
Control Resonant developer Remedy doesn't beat players over the head. It is an open-world game with zones that the player can freely explore, though sometimes it isn't always crystal clear where to go. Control Resonant director Mikael Kasurinen explained on the Dropped Frames podcast (via Kotaku) that it was important for the player to feel like they were figuring out this convoluted world themselves, rather than following flashing arrows. He noted that for players to get the most out of the world, they had to be active participants.
“It’s so important that the players feel like they’re the ones figuring it out,” said Kasurinen. “It’s the job of us as creators to… I mean, it is a crafted experience at the end of the day, right? You have to find the right balance between ‘here’s the world’ and ‘here are the different themes and elements that you have to pay attention to.’ But it has to feel like it’s on you to make a decision on what to do with those elements that you see within the world. If it feels like it’s like ‘go here,’ it’s not anymore a decision for the player. Somebody already decided for you.”
The director went on to note that Remedy recognized that it risked alienating players looking for a more guided and simple experience, but for those that really engage with it, it will be more rewarding and interesting.
“People will be coming back to this game, exploring, trying to kind of find out things and so on," he added. "It’s not something that you kind of go through, you did what you were told, and you’re done. It feels like, no, I made some choices in this game and you have that little little question: Did I make the right choices? And I want that f***ing question. I want people to think like that. I want them to kind of, you know, doubt, go back, check again, see what they could do differently, because that’s life. That’s what makes it sticky and interesting.”
Another developer with a similar philosophy to Remedy's is Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons studio Invoke. Dominic Guay, General Manager at Invoke Studios, told IGN at gamescom 2026 that the developers avoided putting waypoints into the game because they want players to actually explore.
The open-world single-player action-adventure goes easy on the hand-holding by ditching traditional quest markers that guide players directly from one story section to the next. While it does have a compass on the top of the screen — which you can turn off — the player is left to work out where to go by exploring, talking to NPCs, and thinking about what to do next.
“We wanted them to engage with the world, to figure things out and feel that when they found things, it was based on their actions and not just blindly trusting a waypoint,” Guay said.
IGN's Control Resonant review returned an 8/10. We said: "Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse," reads an excerpt from the review. "While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue."
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: The Witcher 3 Remastered brings tons of graphics improvements, but developer CD Projekt Red has left one incredibly important creature as it was: the pigeon.
item.description:
The Witcher 3 Remastered brings tons of graphics improvements, but developer CD Projekt Red has left one incredibly important creature as it was: the pigeon.
Ahead of the remaster's public release, updated pigeon models were found in the game, but it only seems to apply to pigeons that are hanging out on the ground. Still, some people were upset with the assumed change, with one person posting the new ground-based model with the old flying one in a Reddit post captioned, "Gone, but never forgotten."
Luckily, it seems like the beloved low-poly pigeon has survived the remaster, as it was spotted by Kotaku Editor-in-Chief Ethan Gach on X / Twitter out in the wild. Apparently, The Witcher 3 uses different pigeon models for flying and grounded birds! If anything, the low-polygon pigeon looks even funnier in the remaster, as it shows the (lack of) detail even better with the updated lighting.
This is a false alarm.Street pigeons have always been different from the ones flying. https://t.co/flLv1VgqF6 pic.twitter.com/6JFGuzZ7K2
So, even though The Witcher 3 Remastered came with a whole host of graphics improvements, it does seem like some old assets have kept their place in the game. Hopefully, CD Projekt Red also kept in some of the low-detail food in the game as well.
The Witcher 3 Remastered has only been out a few hours, but it's already breaking player records. It's broken the 11-year-old game's peak Steam concurrent player count, and the number looks set to rise further as we get closer to the weekend.
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered is available as a free update on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. To ease you into Geralt’s life on the road, check out the things The Witcher 3 doesn’t tell you, plus IGN’s The Witcher 3 walkthrough and The Witcher 3 endings guide, which outlines all of the major quests and choices in the base game and expansions (now bundled in with the Remastered edition). When you’re ready for the tough choices, check out our The Witcher 3 sex and romance guide to see who Geralt can smooch and all the opportunities to do so. And to make Geralt as strong a monster hunter as possible, check out all the Witcher gear locations, Places of Power locations, and even Gwent card locations.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

Once upon a time, three years ago to be exact, it wasn’t looking like Coyote vs. Acme would ever see the light of day. However, after years of fan outcry, the movie was given a second chance, largely courtesy of a new distributor, Ketchup Entertainment.
After a full theatrical release, the Looney Tunes hit is now available to rent or purchase from digital platforms like Prime Video. The movie is also getting a full line of 4K Blu-rays, now up for preorder.
Coyote vs. Acme is available to rent for $19.99 or purchase digitally for $24.99.
Coyote vs. Acme is a live-action and animated hybrid, sort of in the vein of Space Jam. It stars Wil E. Coyote of Looney Tunes fame who, after decades of brutal injuries on the job, decides to sue ACME Corporation itself. He hires a pretty down-on-his-luck lawyer (Will Forte), and together they take on ACME’s corporate resources, headed by the lawyer Buddy Crane (John Cena).
Coyote vs. Acme was originally produced on a budget of $70 million all the way back in 2023. In 2023, Warner Bros. scrapped the movie, and its reasoning was as simple as a $30 million tax write-off. Yep, it was a Bat Girl situation.
Fans, who were already witnessing Warner Bros. deprioritize its animation slate, weren’t happy. Thankfully, sometimes fans can make a difference.
After years of outcry and a series of coordinated campaigns, Warner Bros. allowed the movie’s creators to shop it to other studios. Ketchup Entertainment ended up swooping in as the savior, announcing a theatrical release for the movie in August 2026.
During its time in theaters, the film managed to gross over $88 million globally, with some reports putting that number as high as $100 million. IGN's review said it "succeeds on just about every level, showing a clear understanding of what makes the classic Looney Tunes characters so timeless."
Our glowing 9 out of 10 score puts it solidly in our list of the best-reviewed movies of the year so far.
The move to digital comes a relatively standard 32 days after the movie’s initial release in theaters. There’s no word on whether it will come to any particular streaming service, but in the meantime, Coyote vs. Acme is available to preorder on DVD, Blu-ray, and 4K.
Warner Bros., on the other hand, is going through more chaos than ever. Paramount has come out on top as the mega-deal’s buyer, and after a brief pause for antitrust lawsuits, the deal is back on track. Paramount execs have mentioned the deal having some stipulations around theatrical releases, so here’s hoping they pay attention to the success of Coyote vs. Acme and are willing to invest in animation.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Game Informer's website and app crashed today amid the debut of its exclusive GTA 6 preview, creating chaos among fans.
item.description:
Game Informer's website and app crashed today amid the debut of its exclusive GTA 6 preview, creating chaos among fans.
Game Informer has released a 14-page cover story with all kinds of new information on GTA 6 today, but unfortunately fans are struggling to access it. The second the story went live, Game Informer's website crashed. Just prior to the release of the coverage, it was confirmed that the story would be made free to all users through Game Informer's app. As you might imagine, this led to the site being overwhelmed with traffic.
It took about an hour for users to start getting into Game Informer's website so that they could read the story. It was chock-full of exclusive details, which we broke down here. Some of those details included confirmation that GTA 6 will feature tropical storms such as hurricanes, something that fans have been speculating about for quite some time.
Although there were a variety of GTA 6 previews earlier this summer, including one from IGN itself, there was more room to breathe. The previews dropped during Rockstar's 27-minute gameplay reveal on Netflix, and there were a variety of outlets and creators with exclusive coverage. It allowed everyone to have some space, whereas this was just one outlet absorbing all of the attention from GTA 6 fans.
As of right now, we're not sure when the next GTA 6 news beat will be. Rockstar has already teased that it will share more about the game's radio stations and music in the coming weeks, and there's hope from fans that we will get one last trailer before launch. Either way, GTA 6 is finally just a little over one month away from launch.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Sony and Nintendo need to make their current consoles last as long as possible amid soaring costs, former PlayStation exec Shuhei Yoshida has said.
item.description:
Sony and Nintendo need to make their current consoles last as long as possible amid soaring costs that have already prompted PS5 and Switch 2 price rises.
That's according to former PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida, who told The Verge that console companies needed to focus on sustaining their current hardware platforms for "as long as possible."
While there's no suggestion that Nintendo plans to launch a Switch 3 anytime soon (Switch 2 only arrived last year!), the company always devotes a chunk of its budget to researching future hardware. And upgrades to the launch Switch 2 model will undoubtedly be considered at some point, similar to the Switch Lite and Switch OLED.
As for Sony, we know that a PlayStation 6 is on the way at some point. Previously, analysts had suggested a 2028 launch seemed likely, though Sony is yet to make any official indication of when PS6 may arrive — and as time goes on, that late 2028 release date feels less and less likely. Indeed, Yoshida has suggested that console makers may now be looking to delay the arrival of next-gen hardware as long as possible.
"Sony and Nintendo have sold enough numbers of their current-generation hardware, so because of the cost of goods, they might be looking [at] pushing back the launch of next gen," Yoshida said. "I think they should try to keep the current generation as long as possible, because people are very happy using PS5 and Switch 2.
"People have [a] finite budget, and it feels like PC and consoles, the components very specific to these devices have increased their price way more than all the other forms of entertainment," he continued. "People who have systems like PS5, Switch 2, or PCs – you know, good enough PCs – probably will be happy to play games on them and not necessarily consider replacing [them]."
The key issue here is the skyrocketing cost of computer memory, AKA "RAMageddon", fuelled in part by the rise of AI datacenters. In short, memory production resources are limited, and much of next year's production output is already spoken for. Should Sony, for example, want to start manufacturing a new console anytime soon, it may be physically unable to do so in the volume it would like — let alone being able to sell the console for a price that consumers would pay.
As a reminder, the Sony launched its PS5 with a disc drive for $500, while its digital-only counterpart sold for $400. These machines now cost $650 and $600 respectively — price rises of $150 and $200 since 2020. PS5 Pro launched at $700, meanwhile, and now costs $900. It's hard to see PS6 arriving at much less than $1,000. Switch 2, meanwhile, has risen in price by $50 since launch last year, from $450 to $500.
And then there's the general lack of desire from both consumers or developers for machines capable of drastically better performance, something Yoshida also noted. The only exception to this is Xbox, which has been more vocal about its push towards a next-gen offering with Project Helix. The difference with Microsoft's team, though, is it has not sold truckloads of consoles of late.
"I don't think lots of people are asking for more power — 'We need more power!' — or even developers," Yoshida concluded. "I don't think developers are asking [for] better hardware! So I think that means that the current generation, Sony and Nintendo are going to do pretty well for many years to come, still.
"Xbox is a team who wants to change the competing landscape, so it's going to be hard for them, but it's their time to play. It's very exciting, what's going to happen next year?"
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social
